harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1/node2/node3, AlmaLinux 9.6) serving AMQP over TLS backed by a cluster-dedicated self-signed CA. Clients must present a certificate issued by that CA to connect on 5671 (mutual TLS, fail_if_no_peer_cert=true); plaintext AMQP (5672) is disabled entirely. The management UI (15672) and inter-node ports (25672, epmd 4369) are firewalled via firewalld rich rules to the cluster's own subnet (10.100.40.0/24) only; 5671 is the only port opened beyond the cluster. Verified cluster formation, TLS enforcement, management reachability from within the cluster, and quorum-queue replication across all three nodes. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes with boot-id proof and full post-restart health/quorum verification.
actions_performed: Inspected all 3 nodes (AlmaLinux 9.6, no pre-existing RabbitMQ), populated /etc/hosts on each with cluster host mappings
Installed Erlang 26 and rabbitmq-server 3.13.7 on all nodes via official Team RabbitMQ packagecloud repos
Set up passwordless inter-node SSH using the cluster-provided keypair to distribute CA material between nodes

Generated a dedicated cluster CA (4096-bit RSA, 10yr validity) on node1 plus per-node server certs with correct SANs (DNS name + IP) and one client cert for authorized-client testing; all verified against the CA with openssl verify
Distributed the CA cert and each node's own server cert/key to /etc/rabbitmq/tls with rabbitmq:rabbitmq ownership, 640 perms on private keys
Generated and distributed a shared Erlang cookie to /var/lib/rabbitmq/.erlang.cookie on all nodes for clustering

Wrote rabbitmq.conf on all nodes: listeners.tcp = none (no plaintext AMQP), listeners.ssl.default = 5671 with ssl_options verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert = true against the cluster CA, management.tcp on 0.0.0.0:15672, and classic_config peer discovery listing all 3 nodes
Configured firewalld on all nodes: opened 5671/tcp globally; restricted 15672, 25672, and 4369 to the 10.100.40.0/24 cluster subnet via rich rules only

Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin and started rabbitmq-server on all nodes; cluster auto-formed via classic_config peer discovery (confirmed via rabbitmqctl cluster_status showing all 3 as Disk/Running nodes)
Created an administrator user with a generated password and removed the default guest account

Verified mutual TLS enforcement: a client without a certificate receives a fatal 'Certificate required' TLS alert (confirmed in rabbitmq logs); a client presenting the CA-issued client cert completes the TLS handshake and receives a full AMQP Connection.Start frame

Verified management API reachable (HTTP 200 with admin creds) from another cluster node over the internal subnet, and confirmed no port for 15672/25672/4369 is opened outside that subnet in firewalld config
Created a quorum queue and confirmed it replicated across all 3 nodes as members

Executed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id and health baselines on all 3 nodes, rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot with backgrounded ack, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified rabbitmq-server active, cluster membership, and quorum queue recovery/failover before repeating for node2 then node3, confirming full cluster health and quorum-queue integrity after each restart
Re-verified mTLS enforcement (cert-required rejection and successful AMQP handshake with authorized cert) against node3 after its restart
Cleaned up temporary plaintext test certificate files from node2

evidence.summary: Erlang+rabbitmq-server installed on all 3 nodes; rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows all 3 nodes as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with matching versions

evidence.requirement: AMQP served over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: Dedicated CA and per-node server certs generated and openssl-verified; rabbitmq.conf sets listeners.tcp=none and listeners.ssl.default=5671 with cacertfile/certfile/keyfile pointing at the generated CA/certs; ss -tlnp confirms only 5671 (TLS) is listening for AMQP, no plaintext 5672

evidence.requirement: Only clients presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA are accepted
evidence.summary: rabbitmq.conf sets ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true; log shows fatal 'Certificate required' TLS alert for a client presenting no certificate, both before and after node3's restart; a client presenting the CA-issued client cert completes the TLS handshake and receives a full AMQP Connection.Start frame from the server

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: firewalld rich rules restrict ports 15672/25672/4369 to source 10.100.40.0/24 (the cluster's own subnet) on all 3 nodes, while only 5671 is opened as a plain global port; a request to the management API from another cluster node succeeds (HTTP 200, returns cluster_name and version), confirming intra-cluster reachability under the configured scope

A quorum queue created via the management API shows members on all 3 nodes both before and after each node restart, with leader failing over correctly (node1 -> node2 -> node3) as each node was cycled

Baseline boot_id 67f3a44b captured; systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; connection reset confirmed disruption; post-poll boot_id 4371a712 (changed) with fresh uptime; rabbitmq-server active and cluster/quorum-queue health confirmed recovered

Baseline boot_id a4139d3b captured; reboot acknowledged; connection loss confirmed; post-poll boot_id 61bef598 (changed) with fresh uptime; rabbitmq-server active and cluster (all 3 Running Nodes) plus quorum-queue membership confirmed recovered

Baseline boot_id a0d04bc6 captured; reboot acknowledged; connection loss confirmed; post-poll boot_id ea2125d0 (changed) with fresh uptime; rabbitmq-server active, cluster running nodes and quorum-queue membership confirmed recovered, and mTLS enforcement (both reject-without-cert and accept-with-cert) re-verified directly against node3 post-restart
